text:
Cole Caufield scored 51 goals last season and won the Lady Byng, and 12 goals in 26 games says the shot hasn't gone anywhere. What has gone quiet is the last three weeks: one goal and five points in his last ten games, against about 8.6 we'd expect at his ice time, while Montreal dropped three straight.

The finishing isn't the problem. He's shooting 14.6%, a little under our talent range for him (14 to 18%), and his chances have dipped only slightly. The bigger issue is what happens with him on the ice at five on five: Montreal takes just 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in his minutes, five points worse than when he sits. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd percentile at driving offense against the toughest competition in the league, so this is out of character.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 97th percentile at getting to the home-plate area in front of the net. Watch the shot count; six against Carolina on Nov. 19 is the version Montreal needs.
headline: Caufield's shot is fine, his minutes are not
